analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) BOJ Recap, 2) GPIF Q&A, 3) TMT Earnings Review and 4) 5 Key Charts 30 Oct 2026
key_insights: BOJ held the policy rate at 1.25% by majority vote, as widely expected. Board member Hajime Takata dissented and proposed a hike to 1.50%.

In the October Outlook Report the BOJ left its growth forecast broadly unchanged, cut FY2026 inflation forecasts slightly and raised FY2027 forecasts slightly to reflect higher crude oil prices since the summer.

The BOJ changed its underlying inflation wording from reaching 2 percent 'between the second half of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027' to underlying CPI inflation being 'at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent'. Price risks stay skewed to the upside and the stance of raising the policy rate toward the neutral rate is unchanged from September.
The BOJ outlook report added a note implying caution on yen depreciation risk from rate hikes by many foreign central banks.

GPIF could not implement an allocation shift before Spring 2027 at the earliest, because its medium-term plan from March 2025 sets an annual verification of the asset allocation at the end of each fiscal year.

GPIF does not need to change its allocation targets for a shift to occur. Current allocations sit at the midpoint of the allowable bands, so it could move toward the outer bounds or allow passive drift as global yields rise.

Raising domestic allocations to the top of the allowable bands would require roughly $90bn of domestic bond purchases and roughly $125bn of domestic equity purchases, based on end-June 2026 holdings. GS says the signal from a GPIF shift matters more than the flow, since it should lead other investors to follow.

GS FX strategy has argued since September that a higher probability of a GPIF flow shift and faster BoJ tightening let valuation play a bigger role in JPY. Short USDJPY is a more attractive portfolio hedge than in recent years, especially if AI-related volatility pushes equities and yields lower together.

Amazon AWS revenue grew 39.3% to $46bn, ahead of consensus but slightly light of whispers. Capex is $220bn this year and 'meaningfully more' in 2027, and management guided AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Inference is well over half of AWS AI revenue.

Amazon advertising grew 12% to $19.6bn versus 18% expected, the first miss in seven quarters. Consumer growth was softer, Q4 sales guidance a touch light and trailing free cash flow was negative $42bn. Prime Day timing explains some of the weakness and management guided advertising back to high-teens growth in Q4.
Intel fell more than 20% overnight and weighed on the broader semiconductor tape. Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn compares with about $17bn expected, due to an operational issue at an Israeli fab.

Intel Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78% with server CPU demand exceeding supply, while PC demand is contracting as memory inflation raises hardware costs. Packaging and fab constraints limit Intel's ability to meet server demand, and the issues may be company specific rather than a secular breakdown in enterprise compute demand.

GS flow desk frames funding and returns on the AI investment cycle as the bigger issue. Advertising misses at Amazon and a peer in search raise the question of whether advertising or the consumer is slowing, and Reddit said 'AI mode does not drive traffic', raising a possible AI cannibalization risk to advertising that GS says is too early to conclude.

Charts flagged: Brazil market expects primary fiscal deficits through 2027 versus government targets of no deficits, GS expects China's current account surplus to widen, Japan trust account net purchases of foreign bonds show no sign of reduced demand, global equities 12m forward P/E ratios are down about 20%, and a GS vs consensus GDP forecast tracker.

market_movers.rationale: AWS grew 39.3% to $46bn with guidance for growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028, but advertising missed at 12% growth versus 18% expected and trailing free cash flow is negative $42bn.
Stock fell more than 20% after Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected, due to an Israeli fab operational issue, while Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78%.

sector_views.rationale: Intel's drop weighed on the broader semiconductor tape, with a negative read-across for PC-exposed suppliers, though the constraints may be company specific.
Amazon's advertising miss follows a search miss from a peer, but Prime Day timing explains part of it and Q4 advertising is guided back to high-teens growth.

Reddit commented that 'AI mode does not drive traffic', cited by GS as a wrinkle for AI and advertising economics.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rate held by majority vote with one dissent for a hike to 1.50%. The stance of raising the rate toward neutral is unchanged.
A hike dissent signals some board pressure for faster tightening.
Reflects higher crude oil prices since the summer. FY2026 forecasts were lowered slightly.
Global equities have de-rated materially, per the GS chart.
